newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's PM to pay day trip to Albania on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Italy's PM to pay day trip to Albania on Sunday.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi will pay a one-day visit to Albania on Sunday, sources at his office said on Friday.
Political sources said Prodi would probably hold consultations in Tirana with Albania's embattled President Sali Berisha and Prime Minister Bashkim Fino.

Italy, with strong trade ties to Albania and anxious to stem an influx of illegal immigrants from across the Adriatic, has played an active part in international efforts to halt the impoverished state's slide into anarchy.

It leads a multinational military force deployed in Albania to safeguard aid supplies. Rioting and looting broke out in February and March when anger at the collapse of investment schemes snowballed into an uprising against Berisha in the south of the former communist country.
France, Spain, Romania, Turkey, Greece, Austria and Denmark also contributed troops to the 6,000-strong multinational force.
Italy championed the installation in March of a national unity government led by Fino under an accord designed to lead to early parliamentary elections on June 29.
